html:
The Kuba Kingdom is a kingdom of central Africa between the Sankuru and Kasai rivers, in what is now the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The map shows it in 1880 and 1900. Tradition says it was united in the early 1600s by Shyaam a-Mbul, a king remembered as a great reformer.

The Bushong people formed its core, ruled by a king called the nyim with a large council of officials. The Kuba are famous for their arts: cut-pile raffia cloth often called Kasai velvet, carved cups and masks, and ndop figures, each portraying a king.

Europeans reached the capital only in the 1880s. The African American missionary William Sheppard arrived in 1892 and later exposed the brutal rubber collecting of the Congo Free State era in Kuba land. The kingdom came under the Free State around 1900 and then the Belgian Congo, and its kingship survives today.
